text: τροφός, a nurse (and thus of a mother who suckles her own children).
τροχιά, (orbita [from orbis], a track; hence) a road.
τροχός, (a wheel; hence) the chariot-wheel of man as he advances on the way of life, following his appointed course.
τρύβλιον, a dish.
τρυγάω, I gather (always of grapes, τρύξ).
τρυγών, a turtledove.
τρυμαλιά, an opening, hole; an eye of needle.
τρύπημα, a hole; an eye.
Τρύφαινα, Tryphaena, a woman-Christian in Rome.
τρυφάω, I live a luxurious life.
τρυφή, luxury.
Τρυφῶσα, Tryphosa, a woman-Christian in Rome, perhaps a sister of Tryphaena.
Τρῳάς, Troas, a harbour city of Mysia.
gloss: Troas, a harbour city of Mysia

text: τρώγω (originally I munch, I eat audibly), I eat. (This word was displacing ἐσθίω in ordinary use.)
τυμπανίζω (from τύμπανον, ‘drum’ used in worship, then ‘implement of torture’), I break on the wheel.
τυπικῶς, either by way of example, or typically, prefiguratively.
gloss: by way of example, or typically, prefiguratively

text: Τύραννος, Tyrannus an inhabitant of Ephesus, probably a rhetorician.
Τύριος, a Tyrian, an inhabitant of Tyre.
gloss: a Tyrian, an inhabitant of Tyre

text: τυφλόω, I blind, make blind, lit. or met.
τύφομαι, intr. I smoke.
τυφόω: pass. I am puffed up, I am haughty.
gloss: I am puffed up, I am haughty
note: headword printed as active τυφόω (passive sense)

text: τυφωνικός (from τυφώς, ‘a vehement wind’); ἄνεμος, a heavy eddying squall.
Τυχικός (or Τύχικος), Tychicus, a Christian of the Roman province Asia.
gloss: Tychicus, a Christian of the Roman province Asia

text: ὑακίνθινος, of the colour of the martagon lily, that is, of a dusky red colour.
gloss: of the colour of the martagon lily

text: ὑάκινθος, a sapphire of dusky red colour like the martagon lily.
ὑάλινος, glassy, transparent as glass.
ὕαλος, glass.
ὑβρίζω, I treat insolently (outrageously), I insult.
ὕβρις, (a) wanton insult, outrage, 2 Cor. xii 10; (b) injury, loss, due to the sea.
ὑβριστής, noun as adj. insolent, insulting, outrageous.
ὑγρός, moist, full of sap.
ὑδρία, a waterpot (hence, of any pot).
ὑδροποτέω, I drink water (alone, not mixed with wine).
ὑδρωπικός, dropsical, afflicted with dropsy.
ὑετός (imber), a shower of rain; rain.
υἱοθεσία, adoption.
ὕλη, wood, timber, brushwood.
Ὑμέναιος, Hymenaeus, a backsliding Christian.
ὑμνέω, (a) intr. I sing a hymn; (b) tr. I praise in a hymn.
ὕμνος, a hymn, especially of praise to God.
ὕπανδρος, under the authority of a husband.
gloss: under the authority of a husband

text: ὑπάντησις, meeting, act of meeting.
ὕπαρξις, a possession, generally of personal property.
ὑπείκω, I yield, submit.
ὑπεναντίος, opposing, hostile; substantive, adversary, Heb. x 27.
ὑπεραίρω, lit. I raise beyond: pass. met. I am exceedingly uplifted.
note: headword printed as active ὑπεραίρω; gloss takes the passive sense (first meaning is 'lit. I raise beyond')

text: ὑπέρακμος, of doubtful meaning; probably of excessive sexual vigour (of the man), rather than past the bloom of youth (of the woman).
ὑπεράνω, far above.
ὑπεραυξάνω, intr. I grow exceedingly.
ὑπερβαίνω, intr. I transgress.
ὑπερβαλλόντως, exceedingly.
ὑπερέκεινος, lit. beyond yonder: τὰ ὑπερέκεινα, the places beyond, c. gen.

text: ὑπερεκπερισσοῦ, most exceedingly.
ὑπερεκτείνω, tr. I stretch beyond the measure assigned to me.
gloss: I stretch beyond the measure assigned to me

text: ὑπερεκχύννω, I pour out so that it overflows.
gloss: I pour out so that it overflows

text: ὑπερεντυγχάνω, I supplicate on behalf of.
ὑπερηφανία, haughtiness, arrogance.
ὑπερλίαν (lit. more than very much): in irony, οἱ ὑπερλίαν ἀπόστολοι, the super-apostles.

text: ὑπερνικάω, I score a heavy victory; I am more than a conqueror.
ὑπέρογκος (lit. of great or excessive bulk), arrogant.
ὑπεροχή, superiority, 1 Cor. ii 1; a position of superiority, 1 Tim. ii 2.
ὑπερπερισσεύω, (a) intr. I abound exceedingly; (b) mid. as act. I overflow.
ὑπερπερισσῶς, most exceedingly.
ὑπερπλεονάζω, I abound exceedingly, I am exceedingly abundant.
gloss: I abound exceedingly, I am exceedingly abundant

text: ὑπερυψόω, I elevate greatly (exceedingly).
ὑπερφρονέω, I have high notions.
ὑπερῷον, an upper room, an upstairs room.
gloss: an upper room, an upstairs room

text: ὑπέχω, I undergo.
ὑπήκοος, obedient.
ὑπηρετέω, I serve, minister to.
ὕπνος, sleep.
ὑποβάλλω, I suborn.
ὑπογραμμός, (properly a piece of calligraphy, a copy, for children to imitate; hence) a model, a type, which has to be followed.
ὑποδέχομαι, I receive under my roof, I welcome to my house, I entertain hospitably.
gloss: I receive under my roof, I welcome to my house

text: ὑπόδικος (a forensic word), liable to (brought under) the judgement of, answerable to.
gloss: liable to (brought under) the judgement of

text: ὑποζύγιον, a beast of burden, either an ass or a mule.
ὑποζώννυμι, I undergird, frap, that is, I fasten cables vertically round the hull of the ship to prevent the timbers from straining or giving way.
ὑποκρίνομαι, I act the part, pretend.
ὑπόλειμμα, a remnant.
ὑπολείπω, I leave behind.
ὑπολήνιον, a wine-press, probably the lower (ὑπο-) trough, smaller but deeper than the ληνός proper, both being cut out of the solid rock.
ὑπολιμπάνω (Ionic form) = ὑπολείπω.
ὑπόμνησις, remembrance, recollection.
ὑπονοέω, I suppose.
ὑπόνοια, a supposition, suspicion.
ὑποπλέω, I sail under the lee of (close to).
gloss: I sail under the lee of (close to)

text: ὑποπνέω, I blow moderately (gently).
ὑποπόδιον, a footstool (of the conquering king placing his foot on the neck of the conquered).
ὑποστέλλω, act. tr. I withdraw, Gal. ii 12; mid. tr. I keep back, Ac. xx 20; intr. I withdraw, Heb. x 38; I shrink from, I shun (c. infin. and answering negative), Ac. xx 27.
ὑποστολή, withdrawal; shrinking.
ὑποστρωννύω, tr. I spread underneath.
ὑποταγή, subordination, subjection, submission.
ὑποτίθημι, (a) I place (put) under some danger, I expose; (b) mid. I suggest, advise.
gloss: I place (put) under some danger, I expose

text: ὑποτρέχω, I run before a wind under the lee of.
gloss: I run before a wind under the lee of

text: ὑποτύπωσις, a figurative representation, serving as an example.
gloss: a figurative representation, serving as an example

text: ὑποφέρω, I endure, suffer.
ὑποχωρέω, I withdraw.

gloss: I strike under the eye, bruise

text: ὑπωπιάζω (from ὑπώπιον, which is from ὑπό and ὤψ, ‘that part of the face under the eyes’), I strike under the eye, bruise; hence, I treat severely, 1 Cor. ix 27, I molest, annoy, harass, worry, exhaust, Lk. xviii 5.
gloss: I strike under the eye, bruise

text: ὗς, a sow.
ὕσσωπος, hyssop. In John xix 29 ὑσσώπῳ is a graphic error for ὑσσῷ (pilum), pike.
ὑστέρημα, (a) that which is lacking, of things or persons; (b) want, poverty, Lk. xxi 4, 2 Cor. viii 14, ix 12, xi 9.
ὑστέρησις, poverty, want.
ὕστερος, (a) comparative, latter; (b) superlative, last, latest.
ὑφαντός, woven.
ὑψηλοφρονέω, I am haughty (arrogant).
ὕψωμα, (a) height, Rom. viii 39; (b) loftiness, haughtiness, (self-)exaltation, 2 Cor. x 5 (but including concrete as well as abstract, whatever is lofty, &c.).
φάγος, a glutton, gourmand.
Φάλεκ (Hebr.), Phalek, son of Eber, and one of the ancestors of Jesus.
gloss: Phalek, son of Eber, and one of the ancestors of Jesus

text: φανερῶς, openly, overtly.
φανέρωσις, a showing forth, with objective gen.
φανός, (a light, a torch; then) a lantern.
Φανουήλ, Fanuhel, Phanuel, father of Anna the prophetess.
gloss: Fanuhel, Phanuel, father of Anna the prophetess

text: φαντάζω, I make to appear; τὸ φανταζόμενον, the appearance.
φαντασία, show, display.
φάντασμα, an appearance; hence a ghost, a spirit.
φάραγξ, a hollow place, a hollow, a valley.
gloss: a hollow place, a hollow, a valley

text: Φαραώ, properly a dynastic title (cf. Decebalus in Dacia, Candace in Ethiopia), but, though sometimes preceded by the definite article, probably everywhere understood as a proper name, Pharaoh, a king of Egypt.
Φαρές (Hebr.), Phares, son of Judah and one of the ancestors of Jesus.
gloss: Phares, son of Judah and one of the ancestors of Jesus

text: φαρμακεία, the practice of drugging, drugging; hence, especially, from the use of mysterious liquids, sorcery, witchcraft, inextricably combined with idolatry.
φάρμακον, a drug; hence plur., of those used in sorcery, and thus sorcery, Rev. ix 21 (v. l.).
φαρμακός (see φαρμακεία), a sorcerer, magician.
φάσις (from φαίνω), information.
φάσκω, I say, either I say frequently, or I allege.
φάτνη, a manger, a feeding-trough.
φαῦλος, worthless, low, paltry, implying not so much what is evil as the limitations and paltrinesses belonging to a low order of things.
φέγγος, a light, ray, beam.
φειδομένως, sparingly.
Φῆλιξ (Latin), Felix, third name of (Marcus) Antonius Felix, procurator of the Roman province Judaea from an uncertain date (before A.D. 52?) till A.D. 59.
gloss: Felix, third name of (Marcus) Antonius Felix

text: φήμη (fama), a report, a rumour.
φθάνω, (a) I anticipate, I precede, 1 Thess. iv 15; (b) I come, I arrive.
φθαρτός, perishable.
φθέγγομαι, I utter (a word), I open the mouth in speech.
gloss: I utter (a word), I open the mouth in speech

text: φθείρω, (a) lit. I destroy, I waste; I damage, injure (in being); (b) usually met. I corrupt morally, I deprave, injure (in character); I seduce, 2 Cor. xi 3.
φθινοπωρινός (derived from τὸ φθινόπωρον, which itself = φθίνουσα ὀπώρα, ‘the concluding portion of the ὀπώρα’), autumnal, in autumn, when fruit is expected.
φθόγγος, a measured harmonious sound, of voice or instrument; an utterance.
gloss: a measured harmonious sound, of voice or instrument

text: φθονέω, I envy.
φθόνος, envy, grudge; plur. where related to various advantages.
φθορά, rottenness, perishableness, corruption, decay, decomposition.
φιλάγαθος, loving what is good.
Φιλαδελφία, Philadelphia, a city of the Roman province Asia.
gloss: Philadelphia, a city of the Roman province Asia
note: this is the place-name entry Φιλαδελφία; the common noun φιλαδελφία is entry 5484

text: φιλαδελφία, love of brothers for each other; hence, love of the brethren, love of fellow-Christians, all being sons of the same Father in a special sense.
gloss: love of brothers for each other

text: φιλάδελφος, loving one’s brothers (fellow-Christians).
φίλανδρος, loving one’s husband.
φιλανθρωπία, (a) love of (for) mankind; (b) humanity, kindness, Ac. xxviii 2.
φιλανθρώπως, kindly.
φιλαργυρία, love of money.
φιλάργυρος, loving money.
φίλαυτος, loving self.
φιλήδονος, loving (sensuous) pleasure.
φίλημα, a kiss.
Φιλήμων, Philemon, a Christian man of Colossae.
gloss: Philemon, a Christian man of Colossae

text: Φίλητος, Philetus, a backsliding Christian at Rome.
gloss: Philetus, a backsliding Christian at Rome

text: φιλία, friendship.
Φιλιππήσιος (Latin [Philippensis], for the pure-Greek Φιλιππεύς, Φιλιππηνός), a Philippian, an inhabitant of Philippi.
gloss: a Philippian, an inhabitant of Philippi

text: Φίλιπποι, Philippi, a great city of the Roman province Macedonia.
gloss: Philippi, a great city of the Roman province Macedonia

text: φιλόθεος, loving God.
Φιλόλογος, Philologus, a Roman Christian.
φιλονεικία (see φιλόνεικος), emulation, rivalry.
φιλόνεικος (φίλος and νείκη [νίκη] ‘victory’), contentious.
φιλοξενία, love to foreigners; entertainment of strangers.
φιλόξενος, friendly to foreigners; hospitable.
φιλοπρωτεύω, I love the first (chief) place.
φιλοσοφία, philosophy, in a bad sense, and perhaps identified with ἀπάτη.
φιλόσοφος, a philosopher.
φιλόστοργος, loving warmly (strongly).
φιλότεκνος, loving one’s children.
φιλοτιμέομαι, (earlier, I am ambitious; then, I act with public spirit; now,) I am zealous, I strive eagerly.

text: φιλοφρόνως, with friendly thoughtfulness.
φιμόω, I muzzle; hence, probably originally a slang use, I silence, φιμώθητι, be quiet! Mk. i 25, &c.
Φλέγων, Phlegon, a Roman Christian man.
φλογίζω, I set on fire.
φλόξ, a flame: πυρός (Hebraistic), a fiery flame: spiritualized, 2 Thess. i 8.
φλυαρέω, c. acc. I chatter (gossip) against.
φλύαρος, chattering, gossiping.
φοβερός, fearful, terrible.
φόβητρον (φόβηθρον, probably more Lukan), an instrument of terror, an object of fear, a bugbear.
